newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods--Gulf, Midco up amid refinery news.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods--Gulf, Midco up amid refinery news.

text.p: Gasoline differentials in Chicago markets blew higher on Thursday in what traders said was heavy buying by Mobil Oil amid unconfirmed talk of a cat cracker snafu at its Joliet, Lousiana, cat cracking unit.
Volatility on the NYMEX, meanwhile, sidelined U.S. Gulf and New York Harbor players, making for a slow day so far.
But developing news about a big fire at PDVSA's 310,000 bpd Curacao refinery may bring players back to the field.

On NYMEX, August gasoline shed 3.50 cents to sit at 66.40 cents and August heating oil dropped 1.23 cent to 54.55 cents. September gasoline fell 0.86 cent to 61.90 cents a gallon and September heating weakened 1.22 cent to 54.90 cents.
MIDCONTINENT

Chicago gasoline differentials were snapped up and driven up by what traders said was heavy buying by Mobil late Wednesday and early this morning. There was unconfirmed talk the company's catalytic cracker at its 203,700 barrel-per-day Joliet, Illinois, refinery was hobbled for unknown reasons on Wednesday.

Late Wednesday, Chicago unleaded gasoline deals were done at 6.00 cents and 7.00 cents, with the 7.00 cents repeated early Thursday. Players said by midday the differentials appeared to begin weakening.
In Group Three, prompt July was considered sold out, and prompt August was pegged 3.00/3.50 cents over September NYMEX. Any months were at 2.25/2.50 cents over the screen.
Distillates were about a half cent weaker, although there was little news.
U.S. GULF
Prompt conventional M1 gasoline differentials showed little movement early Thursday as players stepped back from the market as the underlying futures' prices continued to swing sharply.
"A lot of people are just sitting back watching the screen," one trader said.
But the Curacao fire, which some traders were saying had reduced one of three distillation towers to "a burned crisp," was commanding increasing attention as the session unfolded.
"I can't believe it hasn't had more effect," said one trader.
Prompt conventional M1 gasoline was firmer at as much as 2.00 cents over September NYMEX, compared to 1.25 cents late Wednesday, traders said.
Prompt reformulated A1 gasoline was seen at about 3.00 cents over the M1 price, or about 4.50 cents over the September NYMEX.

Heating oil differentials inched higher early Thursday, with offers for prompt barrels at 2.35 cents under the September futures and any-month barrels at about 2.30 cents under the futures, one traders said.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Activity in the NYH also appeared thin early Thursday because of the volatility on the NYMEX, keeping differentials near flat.

Prompt conventional M2 gasoline futures were talked at about 2.25 cents under the August contract, which reaches its expiration Thursday afternoon. Barrels for early August delivery were seen at about 2.75 to 3.00 cents under the August futures.
Prompt heating oil hovered near 0.20 cent under the August heating oil futures, while low sulphur diesel was put at 1.35 cents over, accordng to market players.
